title: the Gayatri in context
hook: in the Gita, Krishna lists the best of everything. among meters, he names the Gayatri
tomorrow: hymns to Agni, Indra, Ushas, Varuna

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Gayatri in context: in the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad, three lines holding worlds, words and breath, and a fourth foot that's the blazing sun. Did you catch a breath and let it count? Day one thousand two hundred sixty-seven.

Out of all the mountains, which one? Out of all the rivers, which one? Out of all the seasons? In the tenth chapter of the Bhagavad Gita, Arjuna asks Krishna how to recognize him in the world, and Krishna answers with a long list. Among the bodies of water, the ocean. Among trees, the sacred fig. And in the middle of the list, a line about poetry. Among meters, Krishna says, I am the Gayatri. Today: the Gayatri in the Gita, and a look back at a week of placing one verse.
screen: `WHICH MOUNTAIN? WHICH RIVER?` → `KRISHNA ANSWERS WITH A LIST.` → `AMONG METERS, THE GAYATRI.`

segments.voice: In the Gita's tenth chapter, Krishna describes his vibhutis, the ways his glory shows through the world. Of each kind of thing, he names one where he can be seen. In the same verse, chapter ten, verse thirty-five, he says: among chants, I am the great Brihat-saman; among meters, the Gayatri; among months, Margashirsha; among seasons, spring. Notice what he names. Not the verse to Savitr, exactly. The meter. The three short lines from three days ago, the shape the verse is named for. Some readers hear the famous verse in it too, and the Gita leaves room for that. Either way, a meter of the Vedic hymns is held up as a place where the divine shows. That's a fitting end to this week, because the week has been about exactly that: where the verse shows up. It started with the Purusha Sukta, the hymn of the great Person. Then the Gayatri itself. In its own hymn, it's one verse among neighbors, the first verse to Savitr. Savitr turned out to be the god who stirs the day and stills it at evening. The name Gayatri came from the meter, and older law books call the verse the Savitri. In recitation it's framed by Om and three words for earth, the space between, and the sky. The Brihadaranyaka Upanishad read its lines as worlds, words and breath, with a fourth foot that blazes. And now the Gita names its meter in Krishna's list. One short verse, seen from six sides. Next, the Rig Veda's other voices: hymns to Agni, Indra, Ushas and Varuna.
screen: `KRISHNA'S LIST OF WHERE HE SHOWS.` · `AMONG METERS, I AM THE GAYATRI.` · `A METER, NOT ONLY A VERSE.` · `ONE VERSE, SEEN FROM SIX SIDES.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: look back over the week. Settle, and take a few slow breaths. Then let the week's pictures come back one at a time, without hurrying. The verse among its neighbors in the hymn. The weaver rolling up her cloth at evening. Three short lines of eight counts. The ground, the air, the sky. The breath in, out and through. Let each one rest for a breath or two, then let it go. If one stays longer, let it stay. If you pray, you can hold the Gayatri's meaning at the end: may our thoughts be stirred. The bell holds the time.

Your line: the Gayatri in context. Today, pick one thing from Krishna's list, a river, a tree, spring, and when you see it, let it stand for something larger. Day one thousand two hundred sixty-seven.

howItsDone: Hindus who read the Bhagavad Gita meet its tenth chapter, where Krishna names the things in which his glory can be seen, including, among meters, the Gayatri.

myth: in the Gita, Krishna names the Gayatri among meters
chapter ten, verse thirty-five: among meters, I am the Gayatri.
Krishna's list in chapter ten names only gods
it names mountains, rivers, trees, seasons, months and meters too.
in the Gita verse, Krishna names the meter
the Gayatri there is the meter; some readers hear the famous verse in it too.

fork.setup: Krishna is naming where he can be seen, one thing of each kind. he reaches the meters. which does he name?
fork.reveal: the Gayatri. in the same verse he names the Brihat-saman among chants, Margashirsha among months, and spring among seasons.

original.note: Sanskrit: glory, manifestation; the Gita's tenth chapter lists Krishna's vibhutis, the places his glory shows.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Gita and the Gayatri belong to different shelves.
what it means: in the Gita's tenth chapter, Krishna names the Gayatri among meters as one of the places he can be seen.
what a scholar hears: Bhagavad Gita 10.35, gayatri chandasam aham, among meters I am the Gayatri, in the same line as the Brihat-saman among chants.
